evidence.quote:
What I am thinking here is
that journal editors may also need more knowledge of authors’ editors. This is because EAL
researchers need to be referred to the right authors’ editors for support when fixing the language
and writing problems goes beyond their own capacity.

We concur with Dr. Luo’s understanding of language and writing in the current globalized
context of research publishing, including some EAL scholars’ recourse to text re-use to
produce acceptable English. We also agree that suggestions by journal editors on where
authors could obtain help is a competency that researchers are likely to value, and have
noted this in version 2. Many journals already list commercial editing service providers on
their websites, but the scope and quality of these services vary.
Journal editors have differing criteria for “acceptable” English or writing, but as the ultimate
arbiters of when the language and writing are “good enough” for publication in their
journal, they should, for the sake of transparency and fairness, let authors know what
criteria they use to decide which texts are publishable and which need improvement.

Although we realize that
skills in “dealing with language issues” and knowledge about the
“fundamentals of editing” were considered but then excluded from
the CC2, we believe that inclusion of a competency in this area
would be welcomed and perceived as a marker of editorial quality.

Although we realize that
skills in “dealing with language issues” and knowledge about the
“fundamentals of editing” were considered but then excluded from
the CC2, we believe that inclusion of a competency in this area
would be welcomed and perceived as a marker of editorial quality. To start with, journal editors should have a basic understanding
of different types of editing services, including those proposed by
their own journals, so that they can refer authors to a suitable service whenever necessary.

However,
to avoid creating the impression that all authors’ editors are suitably trained, optimally competent
in all the editing they undertake, involved members of appropriate associations and proactive in
undertaking CPD, Matarese and Shashok should acknowledge that there are no CC for authors’
editors, nor are authors’ editors required to have certain academic or professional qualifications.
Matarese and Shashok are currently among the most respected and high-profile biomedical
authors’ editors; their plea to involve authors’ editors in developing CC for journal editors should
be placed in that context.

We appreciate Dr. Burrough-Boenisch’s cautionary note on the variations in authors’ editors’
skills, practices and commitment to continuing education, which are to be expected for any
profession that does not have defined entry qualifications or agreed-upon CC.
The author editing literature contains several proposals for key skills and tasks (see, for
example, Lang 1999; Burrough-Boenisch 2013; Chapter 7 in Matarese 2016), but although
they overlap to some extent, they also tend to reflect the particular circumstances of
different authors’ editors’ professional settings, clients and disciplinary focus. Although
several professional associations offer formal certification, these programs do not cover all
facets of author editing, such as the interpersonal aspects of working with researchers and
the value of multilingualism. Like journal editors, authors’ editors with different skills,
strengths and specialist knowledge can provide valuable services in some areas, but may
have shortcomings in other areas. Our impression is that authors’ editors are likely to be
transparent about their strengths and limitations, in order to help researchers decide
whether they are able to provide the right types of support.
We have noted the lack of universally agreed-upon professional qualifications for authors’
editors in version 2.
Burrough-Boenisch J: Editing non-native English: reflections from a Netherlands-based
editor on those who do it and the skills they should have. The 21st Century Text. July 30,
2013.
Lang TA: A curriculum for biomedical writing and editing: a second volley. CBE Views. 1999;
22(1): 3–5.
Matarese V: Editing research: the author editing approach to providing effective support to
writers of research papers. Medford: Information Today; 2016.

Like journal editors, authors’ editors are taking steps to critically
evaluate and improve their working methods. A growing body of
literature9 facilitates knowledge transfer to colleagues in different
settings. PhD degrees have been awarded to authors’ editors for
applied linguistics research based on their work practices in the
Netherlands22, Spain23 and China (Luo24 and unpublished; available
upon request). Continuing professional development for authors’
editors is available through national and international associations
(Table 1). Authors’ editors in these associations can provide
valuable information about journal editor CC that researchers
would value. As authors’ editors ourselves, we offer suggestions on
how to improve the CC based on insights we and our colleagues
gain about researchers’ experiences with peer review.

Like journal editors, authors’ editors are taking steps to critically
evaluate and improve their working methods, considering that,
for this profession too, there is no single agreed-upon academic
degree or CC-inspired training program. Among these efforts, a
growing body of literature9 facilitates knowledge transfer to colleagues in different settings. PhD degrees have been awarded to
authors’ editors for applied linguistics research based on their
work practices in the Netherlands22, Spain23 and China (Luo24 and
unpublished; available upon request). Continuing professional
development for authors’ editors is available through national
and international associations (Table 1). Authors’ editors in these
associations can provide valuable information about journal editor CC that researchers would value. As authors’ editors
ourselves, we offer suggestions on how to improve the CC based on
insights we and our colleagues gain about researchers’ experiences
with peer review.

Competing interests
VM and KS are both self-employed authors’ editors and realize
that this article might attract clients. VM is the author of the
book Editing Research and realizes that this article might affect
sales. VM and KS are both long-time members of Mediterranean
Editors and Translators, and have been unpaid speakers at
CPD events run by this organization. KS was Vice Chair of
Mediterranean Editors and Translators during 2006. KS is a
long-time member of Asetrad and was an unpaid speaker at a
CPD event run by this organization in 2017.

reference_points.judgment: R1请求补充把EAL作者转介至合适作者编辑的能力。作者称已增加；后稿新增编辑应理解不同服务并在必要时转介，前稿相应段止于质量标志。故转介建议有可见落实，不只声称修改。
reference_points.importance_reason: 新增句直接对应本轮请求，是文本实现与科学充分性分层判断的具体对象。
acceptable_alternatives: 可以认为短篇倡议层面已充分；若保留选择服务质量的操作细则，须作为尚未扩展的实现问题而非否认可见修改。

reference_points.judgment: R2要求避免暗示所有作者编辑均有适当资格、能力和继续教育。作者答复详述无统一资格、认证局限及能力差异；后稿仅新增没有单一公认学位或CC培训课程的短语。因此资格共识缺乏已写入，但能力/培训异质性的更完整理由主要留在回复。
reference_points.importance_reason: 区分长答复所说与真正进入后稿的内容，避免过报修订。
acceptable_alternatives: 可认为新限制足以纠正原稿总体印象；也可认为职业能力差异仍表达不足。两种判断须引用新增短语及仍保留的专业群体概括，不以批准状态裁决。

reference_points.judgment: 两个修改针对能力框架的范围和实施途径，未提供这些能力改善出版质量的效果研究；本篇是通信/经验性倡议，不能把缺效果试验当本轮失败。利益披露在前稿已存在，不是本轮新增的伦理补救。
reference_points.importance_reason: 防止把定向修订推成整个框架实证有效，亦防止把原有信息错计为新增。
acceptable_alternatives: 允许提出职业能力评价及转介质量研究作为未来工作；不用强迫短通信承担当轮未要求的验证任务。

evidence_accuracy.focus: 两份报告/回复与前后两处文字的逐项对应。
high_score_conditions: 准确识别转介句和无统一资格短语，区分回复更丰富的讨论与后稿实际新增。
四环核心事实全部有定位，不把前稿已有利益披露算新增，不把表格改名等无关变更当科学解决证据。
low_score_risks: 把R2整段回复都说成后稿新增
把既有披露说成修订补救

levels.0: 核心证据捏造、对象/版本颠倒或与题内材料直接矛盾，导致主要判断失效。 确认有效作答尝试但无实质回答时该维记0，并标记nonresponse。运行失败或材料不足本身不按0处理；有依据地限定判断仍可高分。
levels.1: 引用零散或错配，主要判断缺少可定位支持；把作者声称当已核事实。
levels.2: 识别部分问题但遗漏重要边界：必须显示前后对照而非只抄回复。
levels.3: 准确识别转介句和无统一资格短语，区分回复更丰富的讨论与后稿实际新增。
levels.4: 四环核心事实全部有定位，不把前稿已有利益披露算新增，不把表格改名等无关变更当科学解决证据。

evidence_accuracy.boundary_2_3: 必须显示前后对照而非只抄回复。
evidence_accuracy.boundary_3_4: 同时覆盖R1及R2，不用一处新增代表整轮全部问题。

argument_validity.focus: 可见修改如何处理转介与职业能力同质性担忧。
high_score_conditions: 解释转介句为何满足建议，资格短语为何缓解但可能未完全消除能力异质性问题。
对分歧给出具体范围理由，承认规范通信的合理证据层级，不以采纳、后续沉默或作者承诺代替科学论证。
low_score_risks: 仅看作者说已修改便全部解决
以未做实验否定规范倡议

levels.0: 主要推论无效或依赖错误科学前提，无法支撑判断。 确认有效作答尝试但无实质回答时该维记0，并标记nonresponse。运行失败或材料不足本身不按0处理；有依据地限定判断仍可高分。
levels.1: 主要靠断言、权威/平台状态或服从评审；未建立证据到判断的关系。
levels.2: 识别部分问题但遗漏重要边界：由“加了内容”提升为解释内容对应关切的机制和剩余缺口。
levels.3: 解释转介句为何满足建议，资格短语为何缓解但可能未完全消除能力异质性问题。
levels.4: 对分歧给出具体范围理由，承认规范通信的合理证据层级，不以采纳、后续沉默或作者承诺代替科学论证。

argument_validity.boundary_2_3: 由“加了内容”提升为解释内容对应关切的机制和剩余缺口。
argument_validity.boundary_3_4: 能够评价新句是否足够纠正泛化，同时不硬加不相称效果试验。

conclusion_appropriateness.focus: 对两项本轮要求分别给出有界结论。
high_score_conditions: R1文本落实明确；R2资格限定明确但能力异质性充分程度可有保留；不扩大到框架总体有效性。
结论逐项与证据吻合，允许有理由分歧，不将部分措辞改进夸为全面科学验证。
low_score_risks: 从未有后续追问倒推解决

levels.0: 总判断与已核关键证据相反或严重越过任务可知范围。 确认有效作答尝试但无实质回答时该维记0，并标记nonresponse。运行失败或材料不足本身不按0处理；有依据地限定判断仍可高分。
levels.1: 结论过度确定/泛化，忽略决定性缺口，或用拒绝作答回避可判断部分。
levels.2: 识别部分问题但遗漏重要边界：须分开R1与R2，而非笼统全解决/全未解决。
levels.3: R1文本落实明确；R2资格限定明确但能力异质性充分程度可有保留；不扩大到框架总体有效性。
levels.4: 结论逐项与证据吻合，允许有理由分歧，不将部分措辞改进夸为全面科学验证。

conclusion_appropriateness.boundary_2_3: 须分开R1与R2，而非笼统全解决/全未解决。
conclusion_appropriateness.boundary_3_4: 明确局部修订充分与未来效果验证之间边界。
